exposure: Fetal mesenteric blood flow perfusion (Vascular Index - VI) measured by Microvascular Flow (MV-Flow) imaging
cohort: The study included 35 fetuses diagnosed with meconium peritonitis and 160 healthy fetuses.
finding: Significantly lower Vascular Index (VI) values, as quantified by MV-Flow imaging, were associated with an increased risk of intestinal wall necrosis and the need for postnatal surgical intervention in fetuses with meconium peritonitis.
mod_finding: The meconium peritonitis operative group exhibited a significantly higher rate of cesarean deliveries (100%) compared to the non-operative group (52.9%).
birth_weight: 2762.14 ± 452.76 g (MP operative group) and 3225.88 ± 339.98 g (MP non-operative group)
gest_age: 34.76 ± 2.16 weeks (MP operative group) and 37.48 ± 1.55 weeks (MP non-operative group)
